Name: welcome to the poppyverse
Description: The Poppyverse's front door -- workplace comedy, growing pains, and everyday life for pilots and their mechanized partners, before things get complicated.

Name: deeper into the poppyverse
Description: Same multiverse branch, deeper layers, fewer safety rails.

Name: sheep milk latte
Description: Retired PILOT and DONOR run a sheep ranch, vend baked goods at farmers markets, and raise kids on bedtime stories that may violate a federal NDA.

Name: lilyverse
Description: DONOR keeps summoning a hologram with a familiar face and voice, and keeps being surprised by how much it still affects her.

Name: spider lilyverse
Description: A reflective branch strung together with spider lilies, gold repair, and the things PILOT and DONOR keep trying to protect for each other.

Name: anomalies in pink
Description: Alternate versions of the same mech souls keep meeting each other across the multiverse to compare notes on their pilots.

Name: apple-y ever after
Description: PILOT and DONOR live ordinary Apple Park tech lives, except reality keeps hairline-fracturing around them into timelines they never expected.

Name: area fifty-done
Description: A top secret research base where the hallways forget basic geography, the elevator remembers people, and the incident log gave up trying to make sense of any of it.

Name: in another world
Description: PILOT and DONOR's regular life, if regular life included extradimensional mech children, cemetery-adjacent small talk, and grocery-store readiness.

Name: innately unabsolvable
Description: The largest branch of the multiverse, and nobody's fully sure why.

Name: things to do in dc
Description: A sightseeing tour of Washington DC where the monuments answer back, the National Mall glows colored light, and the strangest variable is a woman named Iris with a working phone number.

Name: ultravioletverse
Description: Live in the shadows, work in the shadows.

Name: desert roseverse
Description: A sun-bleached branch where the desert mirages aren’t the weirdest thing around.

Name: shibuya-verse
Description: A writer publicly interrogates her own relationship to character arcs, identity, and spectacle, live, in manga panel form.

Name: houston houston
Description: The Johnson Space Center Visitor Center has some unfiled anomalies.

Name: beyond the poppyverse
Description: Where the metaphors go cosmic -- souls, stars, and the site's own thesis statements about what any of this actually means.

Name: fireweedverse
Description: A universe branch grown in the burn scar of Fire Force: spontaneous human combustion, Infernals, Company 8, and the terrible things that grow from bodies the fire did not finish.

Name: psi-verse
Description: A crossover fusion with The Darkest Minds — a federal task force hunts psychic kids who'd rather just be left alone. Somewhere between a jailbreak and a eulogy.

Name: the 43
Description: A half-assed, failed fusion attempt with the 86 (Eighty-Six) universe — we tried to reach 86 but only made it halfway through the fourth wall before getting stuck. 86 divided by 2 is 43. Yay math. Welcome to the 43.

Name: to be hero y
Description: A hero economy runs on belief instead of money, and the newest icon used to be a firefighter with an ordinary apartment and a coffee habit.

Name: tout a toulouse
Description: A French aerospace branch where the callsigns are prettier and the radio still crackles with the same old numbers station.

Name: pelagoverse
Description: A universe branch where PILOT, UNIT, and Sae wash up as marine mammals, adopt a very large stray, and slowly get absorbed into the extended family of an ever-larger sea squirt.
